arrays.title: Building the double array
whereToLook: Check how you split the input string at the commas.
Make sure every comma-separated piece ends up in the array, including ones that fail to parse - those should become 0.0 rather than being left out.
Use a try/catch around Double.parseDouble so a bad value doesn't crash the program.

methods.title: Using separate methods
whereToLook: Each calculation (average, highest, lowest) should live in its own method, not directly in main.
main should call convertToDoubleArray, then calculateAverage, findHighest, and findLowest, then display the results.

input.title: Scanner input and the invalid-input message
whereToLook: Make sure your prompt text matches the challenge exactly.
Check what your program does when the array returned by convertToDoubleArray has zero elements - it should print the invalid-input message and stop instead of calculating statistics.

sourceChecks.name: Uses Scanner
sourceChecks.message: This challenge requires you to use a Scanner to read the space probe data entered by the user.

sourceChecks.name: Has convertToDoubleArray method
sourceChecks.message: Create a method named convertToDoubleArray that returns a double array.

sourceChecks.name: Has calculateAverage method
sourceChecks.message: Create a method named calculateAverage that returns a double.

sourceChecks.name: Has findHighest method
sourceChecks.message: Create a method named findHighest that returns a double.

sourceChecks.name: Has findLowest method
sourceChecks.message: Create a method named findLowest that returns a double.

tests.name: Sample data - statistics header
tests.message: Your program should display 'Space Probe Data Statistics:' before the calculated values.

tests.name: Sample data - average
tests.message: The average of 123.5, 456.2, 789.9, 234.0, and 567.8 should be about 434.28. Check that calculateAverage divides the total by the number of elements in the array.

tests.name: Sample data - highest
tests.message: findHighest should return the largest value from the array built from the entered data.

tests.name: Sample data - lowest
tests.message: findLowest should return the smallest value from the array built from the entered data.

tests.name: Different data set (4 values)
tests.expectedOutput:
Average measurement: 16.0
Highest measurement: 40.5
Lowest measurement: 3.25
tests.message: Your results should be calculated from whatever data is entered, not just the example from the challenge. Check that average, highest, and lowest are computed from the array rather than fixed values.

possibleErrors.message: Your output still shows the example average even though different data was entered. Make sure your calculations use the values entered by the user.

tests.name: Different data set (2 values)
tests.expectedOutput:
Average measurement: 13.0
Highest measurement: 18.5
Lowest measurement: 7.5
tests.message: Check that your program correctly recalculates the average, highest, and lowest for a different set of entered values.

tests.name: Invalid value within the data
tests.expectedOutput:
Average measurement: 15.0
Highest measurement: 30.0
Lowest measurement: 0.0
tests.message: When one of the comma-separated values isn't a valid number, it should be stored as 0.0 in the array (not skipped). Check how you handle a failed Double.parseDouble conversion in convertToDoubleArray.

tests.name: Blank input
tests.expectedOutput: Invalid input. Please provide numeric values.
tests.message: When the entered line contains no data, your program should display the invalid-input message instead of trying to calculate statistics.
